text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high GPU allocation pressure detected in us-west-2. autoscaler failing to add nodes for model-serving-pool-3. current queue depth 142, avg token latency > 1200ms. paging oncall Alex. :rotating_light:
Alex (oncall): seeing it. jumping in now. are we seeing preemptions or quota exhaustion?
Maria: customer reports for the last 8m show elevated 503s for hosted API in west. ticket #INC-8723 opened by support.
Alex (oncall): thanks. oncall takeover. Lee, can you check cluster quotas and preemptions in us-west-2?
Lee: checking nodes and preempt logs. running: `gcloud compute instances list --filter="zone:(us-west2-*) labels:gpu"`
Sam: I'm tailing the autoscaler logs. seeing repeated scale attempts fail with `insufficient accelerators` from cloud provider.
Jordan: confirmed from provider status: spot capacity reclamation in us-west-2 started ~1968004200 UTC. might be region-level shortage.
Alex (oncall): okay, short-term plan: (1) divert new traffic to eu-west-1 fallback pool (2) attempt reserved-pool burst in us-west-2 (3) notify support/customers with interim ETA. Maria, can you draft the customer notif?
Maria: drafting now. posting to #support-alerts and sending to affected corp customers. short note: "We’re routing traffic to eu-west-1 to reduce errors; latency may increase for some customers. Root cause under investigation." :warning:
eng-bot: Action created: #A-1021 - shift-routing-policy to fallback region. assigned to Alex. due 1968005400.
Alex (oncall): executing failover: updating route policy `route:prod->prefer eu-west-1` with dry-run then apply. command: ```
redwoodctl routes update --name prod --preferred-region eu-west-1 --force
```
Lee: I see burst capacity for dedicated customers still available in us-west-2, initiating reserve allocation for model-serving-pool-3.
Sam: autoscaler is still emitting errors. stack excerpt: ```
ERROR autoscaler: failed to provision: provider error: Insufficient accelerators in region
Backoff 30s
```
Alex (oncall): ok applying fallback now. expect propagation in ~30s. changing alerting thresholds to avoid noisy alerts: `gpu-pressure > 120` trigger escalation, keep paging at >200.
Maria: support notified affected customers at 1968004380. some reports say slow token generation; others 503s. log snippet from gateway: `503 upstream overloaded`
Jordan: metrics show eu-west-1 pool handled 70% of new requests after switch, overall errors dropped to baseline in ~90s.
Alex (oncall): nice. marking immediate incident as mitigated for customer-facing errors. still need postmortem and action items. creating incident bridge for detailed triage at 1968004800 UTC.
eng-bot: Postmortem scheduled: 1968008400 (calendar invite sent). Postmortem doc skeleton created at https://docs.internal/postmortems/INC-8723.
Lee: quick note — provider signaled capacity reclaims across multiple instance types; we relied on spot-heavy autoscale for this pool.
Sam: propose change: autoscaler should prefer reserved/dedicated capacity for model-serving-pool-3 when queue depth > 100 to avoid spot churn.
Maria: adding customer impact summary to PM: ~18 customers experienced increased latency; 4 experienced transient 503s for under 3 minutes. tagging CS and account owners.
Alex (oncall): action items (quick list):
1) Alex - confirm route rollback criteria and validate fallback healthchecks. due 1968005400.
2) Lee - raise reserved capacity request with cloud provider for critical instance families, open PR for autoscaler policy change. due 1968080000.
3) Sam - add better backoff/visibility in autoscaler logs + emit `scale_attempt_id` for cross-correlation. due 1968060000.
4) Maria - customer comms and SLA impact assessment; coordinate with Support and AMs. due 1968030000.
5) Jordan - run regional capacity runbook and propose alternate fallback regions for future events. due 1968090000.
Alex (oncall): marking these in tracker. eng-bot created tasks: A-1022, A-1023, A-1024, A-1025, A-1026.
Lee: quick mitigation PR to prefer reserved when queue>100: ```yaml
# autoscaler policy
prefer_capacity: reserved
fallback: spot
thresholds:
  queue_depth: 100
```
Jordan: also recommend adding multi-region pre-fill for cold-start heavy models. small reserved instances in eu-west-1 and ap-south-1 can reduce blast radius.
Sam: running an eval to see token-cost delta with reserved mix. will post numbers later.
Maria: scheduling the 1-hour postmortem: agenda - timeline, customer impact, root cause (spot reclaim + autoscaler policy), remediation plan, owners. invite includes SRE, infra, product, support.
Alex (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll hand this to Maria for postmortem facilitation. Maria — you own the postmortem doc until the meeting?
Maria: yep. I'll collect timelines, embed logs, and list action owners. I'll ping for more context.
eng-bot: Reminder: add the incident tag `capacity-spike` and link the support ticket.
Lee: note for postmortem — include z-init snapshots of `kubectl get pods -A` and `gcloud compute operations list` around 1968004200-1968004400.
Sam: also add a sample of autoscaler request/response with the provider error. makes repro easier.
Alex (oncall): final notes: we kept the API up via fallback, minimal customer impact after routing, but we need to harden autoscaler/reserved mix and reduce dependency on volatile spot pools for critical production models.
Maria: I'll close out the incident thread after postmortem and move action items to the remediation board.
Jordan: assigning myself to runbook update for region-failover checklist. due 1968120000.
Alex (oncall): handing off to Maria for follow-ups. oncall cleared. :white_check_mark:
Maria: thanks — follow-ups documented in the postmortem doc. linking the remediation tracker board: https://remediation.internal/board/INC-8723. please add updates to the corresponding cards.
eng-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> triage -> postmortem_scheduled.
Maria: closing thread. will re-open if anything else pops up. :wave:
